title: The Unclaimed Pedestal

cast.leila: Leila Moss, a municipal exhibition coordinator
cast.tom: Tom Reed, a temporary stage assistant
cast.bev: Bev Ortiz, the exhibition’s accounts clerk

rule: The intact receipt machine prints only on its numbered paper roll; with the roll removed it cannot produce a paper receipt.
deceased: The former caretaker Orson died five years before the exhibition and does not return alive.

chapters.title: A Plinth with No Object

facts.subject: char:leila
facts.anchor: Leila stayed in the exhibition workshop after the morning briefing.

facts.subject: item:delivery_slip
facts.anchor: Leila gave the delivery slip to Tom, who put it in his folder.

facts.subject: org:exhibition
facts.anchor: An eight-pound tape purchase reduced petty cash from seventy-two pounds to sixty-four.

facts.subject: char:tom
facts.anchor: Tom’s badge identified him as the temporary stage assistant.

facts.subject: char:leila
facts.anchor: A stiff shoe raised a small blister on Leila’s right heel.

facts.subject: item:pedestal
facts.anchor: The empty pedestal stood in the exhibition workshop.

facts.subject: char:bev
facts.anchor: Bev was alive and arguing cheerfully with the adding machine.

facts.subject: item:delivery_slip
facts.anchor: The delivery register marked the pedestal unchecked, not missing.

claim: The mayor has already cancelled the exhibition.
“The mayor has already cancelled the exhibition,” Tom said, quoting a message from an anonymous account.
trueClaim: There are sixty-four pounds in the tin.
“There are sixty-four pounds in the tin,” Bev said after making two neat piles.

cognitions.content: The pedestal’s delivery has not yet been checked.
cognitions.anchor: Leila read UNCHECKED in the register and knew it was not a missing-object report.

cognitions.content: The exhibition will expose his inexperience.
cognitions.anchor: Tom believed the exhibition would expose his inexperience, although nobody had criticised his work.

cognitions.content: The spare screws belong to a display attachment.
cognitions.anchor: Bev suspected the three spare screws belonged to an attachment, but had not seen that attachment.
Leila initially misbelieved Tom had ignored the briefing because he kept consulting his folder.

correction.content: Tom consulted the folder because the replacement badge hid the printed instructions.
correction.anchor: When Tom unfolded the badge backing, Leila saw the briefing instructions printed underneath it.

relationship: Leila agreed to work beside Tom instead of sending him away for another badge.
memory: Long before this exhibition, Leila had slept in the civic gallery during a student installation.
hooks: Three spare screws lay taped beneath the pedestal, with no visible sockets to receive them.
The empty object label carried a blue dot that appeared on no public catalogue.
A small bell rang inside the sealed delivery crate whenever it tilted, though the packing list named no bell.
chapters.plan: Tom intended to call the mayor after lunch, but had not dialled the number.
chapters.hypothesis: If the crate held a live performer, the bell might be a signal; nobody opened it on that assumption.
chapters.dream: In a brief doze Leila dreamed that the pedestal delivered a speech, then woke to Tom’s real voice.
chapters.uncertainty: The dot might have been a packing code, but the unsigned label did not establish that.

chapters.title: An Audience for the Wrapping

facts.subject: char:leila
facts.anchor: Leila remained in the civic gallery after the public rehearsal.

facts.subject: item:delivery_slip
facts.anchor: Tom handed the delivery slip to Bev for the reconciliation.

facts.subject: org:exhibition
facts.anchor: A ten-pound deposit refund increased petty cash from sixty-four pounds to seventy-four.

facts.subject: char:tom
facts.object: acting stage manager for the afternoon rehearsal only
facts.anchor: The director appointed Tom acting stage manager for the afternoon rehearsal.

facts.subject: char:leila
facts.object: protected healing blister on right heel
facts.anchor: A fresh pad protected the healing blister on Leila’s right heel; it had not vanished.

facts.subject: item:pedestal
facts.anchor: Tom wheeled the pedestal into the civic gallery and locked its castors.

facts.subject: item:paper_roll
facts.anchor: Leila removed the numbered paper roll and gave it to Bev to count.

facts.subject: item:delivery_slip
facts.anchor: Bev signed the delivery register after checking that the pedestal was intact.

claim: The blue dot means the object is radioactive.
“The blue dot means the object is radioactive,” Tom joked, and immediately said he was inventing that.
trueClaim: The fund is seventy-four pounds now.
“The fund is seventy-four pounds now,” Bev said, matching the refund to the cash.

cognitions.content: He is acting stage manager for this rehearsal.
cognitions.anchor: The director told Tom he was acting stage manager for that rehearsal only.

cognitions.content: A plain explanation will work better than another apology.
cognitions.anchor: Leila believed a plain explanation would work better than another apology, but the audience had not yet arrived.

cognitions.content: The bell belongs to reusable packaging.
cognitions.anchor: Bev suspected the bell belonged to reusable packaging rather than the missing artwork.

cognitions.content: The audience has been told the empty pedestal is the exhibit.
cognitions.anchor: Tom briefly believed, wrongly, that the audience had been told the empty pedestal was the exhibit.

correction.content: The audience was invited to an unpacking demonstration, not an empty-pedestal artwork.
correction.anchor: The invitation corrected Tom’s mistake: it advertised a demonstration of unpacking, not an empty-pedestal artwork.

relationship: Leila let Tom lead the rehearsal and stood ready to answer only when he asked.

memoryRef.anchor: Leila recalled the same student night in the gallery; recalling it did not put her back in that earlier year.

hooks: The workshop diagram showed three holes beneath a removable reading shelf, but the shelf was not in the crate.
A private loan form repeated the blue dot beside an unnamed regional depot.
The unexplained bell sounded again when they tilted the sealed crate for the rehearsal.
chapters.plan: Bev planned to refund the ticket deposits tomorrow; no ticket refund was made that afternoon.
chapters.hypothesis: If the audience refused the demonstration, they would need a new programme; the audience had not voted.
chapters.dream: Tom described a dream in which the mayor arrived disguised as a pedestal; nobody treated it as a visit.
chapters.uncertainty: A muffled sound from the corridor could have been the mayor’s laugh, but no one saw who made it.

chapters.title: What the Public Paid For

facts.subject: char:leila
facts.anchor: Leila stayed in the loading room after the exhibition closed.

facts.subject: item:delivery_slip
facts.anchor: Bev returned the intact delivery slip to Leila in the loading room.

facts.subject: org:exhibition
facts.anchor: The twelve-pound van charge reduced petty cash from seventy-four pounds to sixty-two.

facts.subject: char:tom
facts.anchor: The director appointed Tom display custodian for the exhibition’s remaining week.

facts.subject: char:leila
facts.anchor: By closing time the blister on Leila’s right heel had settled under closed skin, still tender but unbroken.

facts.subject: item:pedestal
facts.anchor: The dismantled pedestal waited in the loading room beside its labelled shelf.

facts.subject: item:paper_roll
facts.anchor: Bev gave the counted numbered paper roll back to Leila.

facts.subject: item:delivery_slip
facts.anchor: The closing account marked the delivery reconciled without charging anyone for a missing object.

claim: We should charge the pedestal an appearance fee.
“We should charge the pedestal an appearance fee,” Tom said; it was a joke, not an invoice.
trueClaim: “Sixty-two pounds remains,” Bev said, closing the actual cashbook.

cognitions.content: The screws secure the removable reading shelf.
cognitions.anchor: Leila watched the three screws secure the reading shelf and knew what they were for.

cognitions.content: The team can admit errors without losing the audience.
cognitions.anchor: Tom believed the team could admit an error without losing its audience; tomorrow’s audience remained unknown.

cognitions.content: The blue dot identifies an old depot route.
cognitions.anchor: Bev suspected the dot identified an old depot route, but the depot’s name was still missing.

cognitions.content: The spare screws proved a part had been lost.
cognitions.anchor: Leila acknowledged her earlier wrong belief that spare screws proved a part had been lost.

correction.content: The screws were packed separately for the removable reading shelf, not evidence of a lost part.
correction.anchor: The packing note corrected that belief: the shelf travelled separately and the screws were deliberately supplied loose.

relationship: Leila asked Tom to write next week’s briefing with her and put both names on it.
memory: Before this temporary job, Tom had been a cinema usher.
hooks: The separate shelf and its packing note explained all three spare screws.
The blue dot’s depot was still unnamed when Bev filed the loan form.
The crate maker’s mark matched a bell-shaped stamp under the lid, but nobody could identify the maker or the bell’s purpose.
chapters.plan: Leila planned to ask the regional depot about the blue dot next week; no answer arrived that night.
chapters.hypothesis: If the bell were an alarm, opening the lid might stop it, but they did not establish any alarm mechanism.
chapters.dream: Leila imagined the pedestal taking a bow and smiled at the image; the actual pedestal stayed still.
chapters.uncertainty: The bell-shaped stamp might be a maker’s emblem rather than an operating instruction.
